questions.question: From which of the Harappan period site has the evidence of an inscription been found?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is  Dholavira . Key Points From  Dholavira , evidence of an inscription has been found. An inscription comprising ten large-sized signs of the Harappan script was excavated from here. questions.question: Pali Texts are associated with which religious literature?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is  Buddhism. Key Points The Buddha delivered his sermons in Pali. The Buddha imparted his lessons verbally through discussion and argument. The talks were not created when he was alive. These were put together by his followers at an elders' meeting in Vesali ( Vaishali ), not Sarnath , after his passing. questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is  Avanti ,  Chedi ,  Vatsa ,  Magadha ,  Anga . Key Points   Avanti was one of the most powerful Mahajanapadas in the 6th century B.C. questions.question: Gold coins issued by the Gupta kings were known as
questions.solution: Solution: Gold coins issued by the Gupta kings were known as Dinaras. Key Points The Gupta gold coins, known as Dinaras, are among the finest examples of numismatics and aesthetic excellence. The governing king and legends were shown on the front of the coins, while a goddess was depicted on the reverse. The emperor is shown with a bow in his left hand on the most popular Gupta currency. questions.question: Who was the Sri Lankan Prince, whose aid was used by the Pallavas to win over the Chalukyas?
questions.solution: Solution: Manavarman was the Sri Lan kan Prince whose aid was used by the Pallavas to win over the Chalukyas. Key Points Manavarman  in Indian sources was the sole ruler of Anuradhapura from 684 AD to 718 AD. He befriended Narasimhavarman I , the ruler of the Pallavas, and served under him. questions.question: Who was the first ruler of the Pala dynasty?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is Gopala . Key Points Gopala  was the first ruler of the  Pala Dynasty . The Pala dynasty ruled the regions of Bengal and Bihar for about 400 years, from the 8th century until the end of the 11th century. Palas followed the Mahayana and Tantric schools of Buddhism. questions.question: Who composed Buddhacharita?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is  Ashvaghosha . Key Points Ashvaghosha was a Sarvastivada Buddhist philosopher and poet . He was born in Saketa in northern India. Though Pali language literature was popular in Buddhism, Ashvaghosha wrote in Classical Sanskrit. Buddhacharita written by Ashvaghosha is an epic on the life of the Buddha.
